reproduction_target: Wet-lab benchtop methods comparison: two tissue preservation methods (fresh vs. flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen), six DNA extraction protocols (PacBio Nanobind, manual CTAB, Omega E.Z.N.A. Mollusc & Insect kit, QIAGEN MagAttract, QIAGEN Genomic-tip, MegaLong), and two post-extraction clean-up kits (Zymo, PowerClean) applied to foot tissue of a single Anodonta anatina individual, scored on DNA yield (Qubit), purity (NanoDrop 260/280), and integrity (Agilent TapeStation / Fragment Analyzer), followed by PacBio Revio HiFi library preparation and sequencing of five libraries on one 25M ZMW SMRT cell. There is essentially no computational reproduction target: the only analysis-shaped operations in the prose are (i) a BLAST comparison of five COI Sanger barcodes against NCBI GenBank for species confirmation and (ii) HiFi read generation via SMRT Link v25.01 on the instrument. All benchtop extraction/QC/library steps are wet-lab (W, OOS for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from the biorxiv JATS XML full text (WebFetch returned HTTP 403; XML retrieved via curl with a browser user-agent, HTTP 200, 73,652 bytes). The paper has NO Data Availability section and NO Code Availability section — this was verified by exhaustive keyword scan of the de-tagged full text for 'availability', 'accession', 'ENA', 'SRA', 'github', 'zenodo'; the only post-Discussion material is 'Supporting information' (Supplementary Tables, Figure S1, Figure S2) and References. No repository is stated, therefore no landing page or README was fetched (per protocol, absence of a stated repo is a finding, not a trigger to search the web). Only 2 steps are computational (C1 BLAST, C2 SMRT Link HiFi generation); 6 coarse wet-lab steps counted in W and not verdicted. Boundary call recorded under capture_claim.

steps.label: BLAST of five COI Sanger barcodes against the NCBI GenBank database to confirm morphological species identification as Anodonta anatina — no BLAST program name/flavour (blastn?), no version, no e-value/identity thresholds, no database snapshot date, no query sequences deposited

PacBio HiFi read generation: sequencing run set up with SMRT Link v25.01 on a Revio platform (Revio SPRQ sequencing plate, one 25M ZMW SMRT cell, 30-hour movie, 2-hour pre-extension); HiFi consensus/read-length and quality metrics reported in Table 3 — closed vendor software, no read data deposited to SRA/ENA/any archive

Field sampling of five adult Anodonta anatina by snorkeling in Türlersee, Switzerland (permit Nr. 24091, 2024-08-05) and live husbandry at the Eawag Aquatikum facility (19 °C, open-water circuit, fed lab-grown algae twice weekly)

COI barcoding wet-lab: foot biopsy, E.Z.N.A. Tissue DNA kit (Omega Bio-tek) extraction, NanoDrop Eight QC, PCR with primers LCO22me2 / HCO700dy2 under stated cycling conditions, product purification and Sanger sequencing by Microsynth AG

Six DNA extraction protocols on ~30 mg foot tissue from a single individual, each on fresh and on flash-frozen (liquid nitrogen, −80 °C) tissue, in triplicate (duplicate for GenomicTip and MegaLong on frozen tissue), per manufacturer protocols; TissueRuptor II homogenisation for Nanobind and Omega
Post-extraction clean-up of CTAB and Nanobind fresh-tissue extracts with two commercial kits (Zymo, PowerClean)

DNA quality control on three metrics with stated success thresholds: yield (Qubit dsDNA HS kit, >1 µg), purity (NanoDrop 260/280 between 1.8 and 2.0), integrity (Agilent TapeStation gDNA ScreenTape, largest peak >15 kb); second-round QC at the GTF facility on a 5200 Fragment Analyzer

PacBio library preparation at the Lausanne GTF: short-read eliminator (SRE) kit, Megaruptor 3 shearing to 15–20 kb target (Omega_frozen1 not sheared), fragment profiling on Fragment Analyzer (HS large fragment 50 kb kit), repair/A-tailing/SMRTbell adapter ligation/nuclease treatment per SMRTbell prep kit 3.0, primer annealing and polymerase binding with the Revio SPRQ polymerase kit

headline.static_readiness: 0/2 (0%) — stage1 ceiling only, no R★ (R★ needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: X on both computational steps; the inference-inclusive upper bound does not rise above X at stage 1 and cannot rise at stage 2 either, because the blocker on both steps is the data axis, not the code axis. Neither the five COI Sanger barcodes (C1 input) nor the 91 Gb of PacBio HiFi reads from five libraries (C2 output, tabulated in Table 3) are deposited in any archive — the paper has no Data Availability statement at all — so no input to either step is obtainable. There is likewise no code repository of any kind, no environment lockfile, container, or conda spec. The single exact version pin in the whole paper (SMRT Link v25.01) attaches to closed vendor instrument software whose inputs are unavailable, so it buys no readiness. This is a benchtop protocol-comparison paper whose scientific claims are wet-lab claims (yield/purity/integrity/sequencing output across extraction protocols); computational reproduction is essentially not a meaningful target here, and the 0/2 static readiness should be read as OOS-dominated rather than as a computational-quality failure.
headline.coverage: 2 computational steps assessed from biorxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose (BLAST species confirmation; SMRT Link v25.01 HiFi read generation). 6 coarse wet-lab steps (field sampling/husbandry, COI barcoding bench work, six DNA extraction protocols × two preservation methods, two clean-up kits, DNA QC, PacBio library prep) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: Whole paper — there is no Data Availability section
gaps.missing: No data accession of any kind is stated. The five COI barcode sequences used for species confirmation (C1) are not deposited in GenBank/ENA despite being BLAST-compared against GenBank. The 91 Gb of PacBio HiFi reads from five libraries, whose per-library yield, read length, and Q-values are the paper's headline quantitative result (Table 3), are not deposited in SRA/ENA/DDBJ. The per-replicate DNA QC measurements exist only inside Supplementary Table S1 and Tables 1–3 (no machine-readable archive, no raw TapeStation/Fragment Analyzer traces beyond figure panels S1/S2).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the five COI barcodes in GenBank with accessions, deposit the five PacBio HiFi read sets in SRA/ENA under a BioProject, and archive the raw QC measurement tables and instrument traces (TapeStation, Fragment Analyzer, Qubit, NanoDrop) as a machine-readable dataset (e.g. Zenodo/Dryad) with a DOI cited in the paper.

gaps.where: Whole paper — there is no Code Availability section
gaps.missing: No repository (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage) is stated anywhere. No scripts exist for the BLAST species assignment, for the summarisation of QC metrics into the success/failure colour coding of Figures 2 and 3, or for the generation of any figure or table.
gaps.how_to_close: If any scripting was used to assemble Figures 2/3 and Tables 1–3 from raw QC output, publish it in a public repository with an archived DOI. If the analysis was entirely manual/spreadsheet-based, state that explicitly and deposit the spreadsheets.

gaps.missing: No version pin: the BLAST program flavour is not named (only 'the Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST)'), no version number is given, and no GenBank database release/snapshot date is recorded. The step is version-floating and caps at NI on the version axis even before the data-axis zero applies.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the exact program and version (e.g. blastn 2.15.0+) or the web-BLAST access date, and record the GenBank/nt release used.

gaps.missing: NCBI BLAST as used here is a closed hosted web service against a continuously-updated database. Even with the query sequences in hand, the assignment is not re-derivable to the same output because the reference database has moved on and no snapshot identifier or query date is recorded.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the query date and the exact database release, or run a local blastn against an archived, checksummed nt/mito reference and publish that reference's identity.

gaps.missing: No search parameters at all: no e-value threshold, no percent-identity or query-coverage criterion, no statement of how many top hits were inspected or what decision rule assigned each of the five individuals to A. anatina.
gaps.how_to_close: State the search parameters and the explicit assignment criterion (e.g. top hit >99% identity over >95% query coverage), and report the per-individual hit table.

gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind — no container digest, no conda/env spec, no lockfile, no requirements file. The single exact version string in the paper (SMRT Link v25.01) is an instrument-software pin with no surrounding dependency closure, so version stays at 1 for C2 and there is no closure to verify at stage 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Not meaningfully closable for vendor instrument software; for the BLAST step, provide a container digest or conda-lock pinning blast+ and the reference database version.

gaps.missing: Field sampling and husbandry, COI barcoding bench work, six DNA extraction protocols across two preservation methods in triplicate, two post-extraction clean-up kits, DNA QC on four instrument types, and PacBio library preparation are physical benchtop steps, out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W (6), not verdicted. These six steps carry essentially all of the paper's scientific content — the protocol comparison itself is the result.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. Wet-lab reproducibility here would be addressed by protocols.io deposition of the manual CTAB protocol and the kit deviations (single final elution for Omega; TissueRuptor II homogenisation), and by the per-replicate raw QC data called for under gap type 1.
